notes: Liaoshi 2 explicitly names Saladi (撒剌的), Emperor Taizu's father, while chapters 56 and 59 infer the same father as the elder brother of Taizu's paternal uncle Shulan. Chapter 60 attributes the same early Khitan industrial program to Saladi.

The forms 剌哥 and 剌葛 refer to Cige or Lage, Emperor Taizu's younger brother and the leader of the AD 911-917 rebellion. Liaoshi 1 follows the same rebel continuously and records his renaming as Baoli; chapter 56 identifies him by the same sibling relationship and surrender.

These records identify Empress Chunqin of the Shulü clan, also titled Empress or Empress Dowager Yingtian, Taizu's consort and the grandmother whom Wuyu confined after taking the throne. The Liaoshi records supply her posthumous and honorific titles; the two Wudai histories preserve the Shulü clan form and the same Wuyu episode.

Liaoshi 6 explicitly states that Emperor Muzong's personal name was Jing and his childhood name was Shulü. Xinwudaishi 73 identifies the Prince of Qi Shulü as Deguang's son, records his accession after Wuyu, and says he was later named Jing; chapters 12 and 70 refer to that same reigning Shulü in AD 959 and during his AD 951-968 reign.
Taizu's paternal uncle Shulan (述瀾), Empress Chunqin of the Shulü clan (述律氏), and Emperor Muzong whose childhood name was Shulü (述律) are three distinct members of the early Liao ruling family.
